solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put out for the count? It would be mad to get up

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: nuts is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A boxer flattened for a count of ten would be crazy to climb back to their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark ends the definition; the second sentence is the wordplay, with STUN reading upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to knock them senseless, as a boxer is when floored and counted out.

clue.text: Relatively broad cross carried by old man over crates

indicators.note: in a down clue, something carried by another sits on top of it, so it comes first
to crate something is to pack it inside a box, so this word holds the others within it

blocks.note: over as in finished
a cross is the letter X
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: An angry old man is carrying crates, perhaps getting broader across the shoulders from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like a direction but means finished, and it is the outer shell around the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something expanded has been made wider or larger in comparison with before, so it is broad by comparison.

clue.text: Disarming location? Nodding head in doubt on breaking ice

indicators.note: a nodding head bobs back and forth, so the front letters of the following word swap places
breaking into something puts one piece inside the other

blocks.note: something in doubt is unclear
to ice is to freeze
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone nods uncertainly while ice cracks beneath them, at some place that disarms.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first two letters of the word for doubt change places; the rest stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone free of atomic weapons is a place where disarmament has happened, hence a disarming location in the cryptic sense.

clue.text: Is about to trade 100%? 10 out out of 10? With capital, more would want these

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written
to deal is to trade

blocks.clueFragment: With capital, more would want these
blocks.note: no letters: an extra hint, since More with a capital M is Thomas More, whose Utopia pictures a perfect society

explanation.surface: A trader asks whether a full hundred per cent is on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The last sentence is an extra hint: with a capital, More is Thomas More, author of Utopia, who would want ideals. The doubled 'out' is in the source.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are standards of perfection, and full marks or a complete score are figures for being perfect.

clue.text: Visual basis for Dilbert’s action, or analysis of argon in school?

indicators.note: analysing something breaks it down into parts, so the letters are taken apart and rearranged
in places the rearranged letters inside the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: Either a picture behind a cartoon character's office life or a chemistry lesson on argon at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Dilbert is an American comic strip satirising office hierarchies. GAM, a school of whales, is a word few solvers know.
explanation.definitionFit: An organogram is a chart of an organisation's structure, the office hierarchy that drives the Dilbert cartoons.

clue.text: We look as though we’re going about a restoration of machinery or wheels

definitions.text: We look as though we’re going about

indicators.note: to wheel is to turn round and round, so the letters are spun into new order

blocks.note: taken as written
a refit restores machinery to working order
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some creatures speak, saying they seem to be on the move while a machine is restored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheels' looks like the noun at the end of a list, but it is a verb telling you to turn the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotifers are tiny water animals whose crowns of beating hairs look like spinning wheels, so they appear to be rotating.

clue.text: Rules on air that smoker will resent

indicators.note: on air means broadcast, so we go by how the word is spoken

blocks.note: syntax is the set of rules for building sentences

explanation.surface: Regulations announced on the radio that annoy smokers.
explanation.walkthrough: A sin tax is a duty on things like tobacco and alcohol, which smokers resent paying.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy on vices such as cigarettes falls on smokers, who naturally begrudge paying it.

clue.text: Suddenly see timeless Arctic Circle

indicators.note: timeless means without time, whose abbreviation is T, so that letter goes

blocks.note: to intuit is to grasp something in a flash

explanation.surface: Someone suddenly glimpses the eternal Arctic Circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arctic Circle' looks like the line of latitude, but a circle here is a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are the indigenous peoples of the far north, a community or circle living in the Arctic.

clue.text: Current, unforeseen new Tudor building …

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters are put together in a new way

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unexpected trend is emerging for new Tudor-style houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present-day; it is a flow of water. The ellipsis carries this answer into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertow is a hidden flow of water beneath the surface, pulling against the waves, so it goes unseen.

clue.text: … which might be one if it does this run

definitions.text: which might be one if it does this

blocks.clueFragment: which might be one if it does this
blocks.note: first meaning: the previous answer, if its last three letters swapped round, would read as a phrase for a number below two
second meaning: flee from danger

explanation.walkthrough: 'Which' is the answer to 9 across: if it rearranges the end of itself, TOW becomes TWO, giving UNDER TWO, and one is under two.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is an idiom for retreating or running away in fear.

clue.text: Inability to coordinate actions of drinkers that were thrown out of cab?

indicators.note: the people put out of the vehicle end up outside it, on either side

blocks.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, a group of former heavy drinkers
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: Drunks being thrown out of a taxi because they can't control their movements.
explanation.walkthrough: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, ironic for drinkers who can't stand up straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Ataxia is the medical term for loss of muscle control, so movements become clumsy and uncoordinated.

clue.text: Used to breed domestic animals, yielding first in championships and No 2 – but not No 3

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word that follows is the one picked out
yielding means giving up, so a letter is surrendered
not the third means the letter in third position is dropped

blocks.note: cats are household pets
the opening letter
number two is a childish word for faeces

explanation.surface: Pets at a show give up first place in the championships and settle for second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 2' looks like a runner-up, but it is a euphemism; 'No 3' then means its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal at stud is kept for mating, so it is being employed for breeding purposes.

clue.text: A Merlot upset by drunken Don, quite shaky in the bar

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and jumbled
a drunk staggers about out of order, so these letters are rearranged too

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunken man named Don knocks over a glass of Merlot in a pub, looking unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub, but it is a musical bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremolando is a musical direction for a trembling, quavering effect, so the notes in that measure sound shaky.

clue.text: Engine experts taking gloves off African flyer

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are shuffled

blocks.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British motoring breakdown service
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mechanics remove their gloves before working on an African aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, whose patrols fix broken-down cars.
explanation.definitionFit: The aasvogel is a South African vulture, so it is a bird that flies over Africa.

clue.text: Work freehand to do the curtains

indicators.note: to work material is to shape it into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sews or paints window curtains freehand, without a pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtains' looks like drapes but is slang for the finish, as when a play's curtain comes down.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtains is slang for the finish or death, and the end of the road means the final point.

clue.text: Play up?

blocks.note: surface reading: misbehave, as a child or a machine does
setter's reading: play is free space to move, and up means overhead

explanation.walkthrough: Play here is a noun, the slack or space that lets something move, as in play in a steering wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Headroom is the clear space above one's head, so it is room to move in an upward direction.

clue.text: He doesn’t think to resettle in Hobart

indicators.note: resettling moves things to new positions, so the letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: taken as written; Hobart is the capital of Tasmania

explanation.surface: An impulsive man moves to Hobart in Tasmania without thinking it through.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotbrain is an archaic word for a rash, hot-headed person who acts before considering.

clue.text: Fat revolutionary loves occupying bit on the side of Kent?

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters run backwards
occupying a place means being inside it

blocks.note: nil and O, two words for zero, which is love in tennis

blocks.clueFragment: bit on the side of Kent
blocks.note: Lois Lane is the girlfriend of Clark Kent, Superman

explanation.surface: A rebel's lovers set up home in a scrap of land beside the county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent looks like the English county, but it is Clark Kent, and Lois Lane is his romantic interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanoline is a greasy substance taken from sheep's wool, a kind of fat used in ointments.

clue.text: Where Giants made a Causeway with one-for-one fit

indicators.note: one for one means swapping one character for another that also stands for one

blocks.note: the Giant's Causeway is in County Antrim, Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Legend tells of giants building a causeway, a fitting tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Both A and I can mean one; the I replaces the A at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in trim is in good physical condition, so they are healthy and fit.

clue.text: Love apple core to be spewed out by robots?

indicators.text: core to be spewed out by
indicators.note: only the inner part of the following word is kept, its outer letters thrown away

blocks.note: robots are automatons, and its central six letters are kept

explanation.surface: Machines spit out the core of an apple, which they cannot stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that robots must first become AUTOMATONS before the middle is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Love apple is an old name for the tomato, once thought to be an aphrodisiac.

clue.text: Lady of the Night at first royally entertained by Jethro

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of the word is taken
a guest entertained by a host is held within their home

blocks.note: opening letter
Jethro Tull was an agricultural pioneer, and a rock band took his name

explanation.surface: A noblewoman of the evening is grandly hosted by a man named Jethro.
explanation.walkthrough: Naming only the first name, Jethro, the setter expects the famous surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A trull is an archaic word for a prostitute, a woman working at night.

clue.text: Esther Rantzen’s straying!

indicators.note: the possessive says the answer belongs to, and is held within, the name before it

blocks.note: the end of the first name runs into the start of the surname

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style exclamation that the TV presenter Esther Rantzen is being unfaithful.
explanation.walkthrough: Esther Rantzen is a British television presenter, famed for consumer show That's Life and founding ChildLine.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means wandering from the proper course, so it describes someone who strays.

clue.text: Start of Operation Midnight?

blocks.note: first meaning: the time a military attack is set to begin
second meaning: on the 24-hour clock midnight is 00:00

explanation.surface: Code name for a military mission launched at midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of' looks like it takes the first letter, O, from Operation, but it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero hour is when a planned attack begins, and midnight reads as hour zero on a twenty-four-hour clock.

clue.text: One who entertains a large group of people

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who receives guests
second meaning: a great crowd or multitude

explanation.surface: A party giver throws a do for a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the person welcoming guests at a party and a great number, as in a host of admirers.

clue.text: Bearer of warning maybe so daring to violate

indicators.note: violating something does violence to it, wrecking its order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning messenger is so bold as to break the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic notices such as those for bends or falling rocks carry cautions to drivers; maybe signals that not all such boards are hazard alerts.

clue.text: The thing, I stress, is left for disposal

indicators.note: things set out for disposal are arranged or dealt with afresh

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone insists that an object has been put out with the rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I stress' looks like a speaker's aside, but it belongs to the definition: an emphatic way of saying it.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun is used for emphasis, the object itself, meaning that very object and no other.
